question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: NVDA's last 5 guide cycles. Beats of the guidance midpoint ran 4.6-5.7% (Q3FY26 57.0 vs 54; Q4FY26 ~68.1 vs 65; Q1FY27 81.6 vs 78; Q2FY27 96.2 vs 91), implying a Q3 actual of ~$113.5B. Next-quarter guide / prior actual ran 1.115-1.156, easing lately to 1.115 and 1.123; ~1.12 x 113.5 = ~127. The guide midpoint rose by +11, +13, +13 and +17B; another +17 to +22B gives 125-130. Upside: management flagged hyperscaler demand picking up more in Q4, and China DC is excluded so any inclusion lifts the guide. Downside: supply/ramp constraints or a more conservative guide. Markets: only thin Polymarket contracts on Q3 data center revenue (imply a DC median of ~$105B, consistent with total ~$112B), not matching this contract, so used as evidence, not an anchor. No market prices the Q4 guide itself.
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 (NVDA PR, 2026-08-26): revenue $96.2B (+18% q/q, +106% y/y); Data Center $89.0B; Q3 FY27 guide $108.0B +/-2% (range 105.8-110.2), China DC compute excluded, GM 74.0%.
- Q1 FY27 (NVDA PR, 2026-05-20): revenue $81.6B (+20% q/q); Q2 guide $91.0B +/-2%. Q2 actual beat the guide by +5.7%.
- Q3 FY26 (CNBC, 2025-11-19): actual $57.0B vs guide $54B (+5.6%); Q4 FY26 guide $65B (1.14x the prior actual). Q4 FY26 actual ~$68.1B and Q1 FY27 guide ~$78B are from memory (beat ~4.8%; guide ~1.145x the prior actual).
- Guide / prior-quarter-actual ratios: Q3FY26 ~1.156 (54/46.7), Q4FY26 1.14, Q1FY27 ~1.145, Q2FY27 1.115, Q3FY27 1.123.
- Step-ups in guide midpoint: +11, +13, +13, +17 ($B).
- Fool (2026-09-15): NVDA has exceeded the high end of its guide 12 straight quarters, averaging 3.1% above the high end over the last 4. Management: ACIE drives Q3 DC growth; hyperscaler demand could pick up more strongly in Q4.
- Q3 FY27 analyst consensus ~$111.3B (MarketBeat/search snippet, Oct 2026), revised up 5.7% over 3 months. Q4 consensus searched for but not found (Chartmill returned 403).
- Polymarket has thin markets on Q3 data center revenue only (not the Q4 guide).
- Status quo: NVDA issues a single-point +/-2% guide; the midpoint resolves.
- Resolves off the Outlook section of the Q3 FY27 press release (due 2026-11-17 after close), not the actual Q3 revenue. Rounded to the nearest $1B.
- Event window: the single release on 2026-11-17; as of 2026-10-23 the release has not occurred (0% elapsed).
- Risks both ways: China DC inclusion (up), Rubin ramp/supply constraints (down), conservatism in guidance (down).
calls.reference_class: NVIDIA quarterly revenue guidance midpoints FY26-FY27: guide = prior-quarter actual x (1.11-1.16), where the actual typically beats the prior guide by 4-6%

calls.reasoning: Anchor: Yahoo consensus for the Jan-2027 quarter is $124.5B (42 analysts, range 117-138). NVDA has guided above consensus in each recent quarter (Q3 $108B vs $104.2B expected; Q1 $78B vs ~$69B expected) and beaten its own midpoints by ~3-5%. If Q3 actual is ~$111-113B and the guide implies 10-14% sequential growth, the midpoint is ~$122-129B. The Rubin ramp (shipping since August, supply-constrained) and a ~70% FY28 growth outlook support the upside. Risks are supply/yield limits, conservative guiding with China excluded, and margin pressure. No human market prices Q4 guidance: Polymarket only has thin Q3 Data Center revenue contracts and Manifold has a Q3 revenue market, neither of which matches this question.

A 12-15% step on that gives a Q4 guide of about 126-130B. Consensus for Q4 revenue is ~124.5B, and the Q3 guide came in ~4% above its consensus, which suggests ~129B. The FY28 $690-700B outlook and the Q4 gross margin trough (a product ramp) add upside tail. Supply constraints are the main downside. No market prices the Q4 guide directly; the Polymarket contracts are on Q3 Data Center revenue and are only evidence about the Q3 actual.

calls.reasoning: The Q3 actual is projected at about $113.4B from NVDA's 4.6-5.7% beats of its guide midpoints over the last four quarters. Recent next-quarter guides ran 1.115-1.123x the prior actual, which gives about $127B. Guides have come in above consensus (Q4 consensus is $124.5B, and the Q3 guide was about 4% above its consensus), which suggests about $129B, but consensus tends to move up after a beat. Upside: the Rubin ramp and China data center revenue being added back. Downside: supply limits and conservative guiding. No market prices the Q4 guide.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the method (Q3 actual x step ratio, cross-checked against consensus) and differed only by about 2.5B at the median. Factual dispute over the Q3 consensus (108.98 Yahoo vs 111.3 MarketBeat snippet): could not be settled without web access; it matters little because the projected Q3 actual (about 113.4B, from the beat pattern and consistent with Manifold's 112-113B) drives the median. Q1 actual 81.5 vs 81.6: immaterial. Judgment: recent step ratios (1.115-1.123) weighted more than the consensus-gap method, with a slight upward lean for the Rubin ramp. Carried forward the reference class and a dispersion of about 11-12 from the runs.
